title: 맛있겠어요! 제가 하겠습니다: 짐작과 약속
objective: By the end, you can attach -겠- to verb and adjective stems, use it to make a guess (맛있겠어요) or a promise (제가 하겠습니다), and understand everyday set phrases like 알겠습니다.
summary: Learn the two main uses of -겠-: guessing from what you see or hear, and saying what you will do.

task.title: Guess, promise, and ask
task.line: Read each situation, then choose, fill in, fix, or write the -겠- form that fits.

forms.when: You see, hear, or are told something now and make a guess. Add 겠 straight to the stem: 맛있- → 맛있겠어요, 바쁘- → 바쁘겠어요.
forms.means: It looks… / It must be… / I bet…
forms.exampleMeaning: Wow, this cake looks really delicious!

forms.when: Saying what I will do: a promise, a plan, or an offer. Subject is 'I' (제가/저는). -겠습니다 is formal, common at work.

Politely asking what the listener wants to do. Very common in shops, cafés, and restaurants. Stem ending in a consonant: add 으 (앉으시겠어요). ㄹ-stems drop ㄹ and take no 으 (만들다 → 만드시겠어요). For eating and drinking, use the honorific verb 드시다 (드시겠어요).
forms.means: Would you like to…? / Will you…?
forms.exampleMeaning: What would you like to have, sir/ma'am?

forms.when: Fixed polite phrases you hear every day. Learn them as whole chunks.
forms.means: 잘 먹겠습니다 (said before eating), 알겠습니다 (I understand / Got it), 처음 뵙겠습니다 (Nice to meet you)

watchOut: 좋으겠어요 (X) → 좋겠어요 (O): -겠- never takes 으. Add it straight to the stem.
바빠겠어요 (X) → 바쁘겠어요 (O): Do not change the stem to the 아/어 form first. 바쁘- + 겠 = 바쁘겠어요.
저는 배고프겠어요 (X) → 저는 배고파요 (O): You know your own feelings, so don't guess about them. Use -겠- for other people's feelings.
가겠요 (X) → 가겠어요 (O): After 겠, the polite ending is always -어요.
exercises: Is -겠- a guess or 'I will'? Write Guess or Will: ① (사진을 보고) 거기 날씨가 덥겠어요. ② (회의에서) 제가 내일 전화하겠습니다. ③ 구름이 많아요. 곧 비가 오겠어요. ④ 다음 주에 다시 오겠습니다.
Fill in the blank with the -겠어요 form of the word in brackets: ① A: 저 어제 세 시간 잤어요. B: 정말 ____ (피곤하다) ② 이 가방 아주 커요. ____ (무겁다) ③ A: 요즘 일이 아주 많아요. B: ____ (바쁘다)
Find and fix the mistake: ① 와, 이 옷 정말 좋으겠어요. ② 저는 지금 배고프겠어요.
Answer your boss with -겠습니다: ① 상사: 이메일 오늘 보내 주세요. 나: 네, 오늘 ____ (보내다) ② 상사: 내일 일찍 오세요. 나: 네, 내일 일찍 ____ (오다)
You work in a café. Ask the customer politely with -(으)시겠어요: ① 커피 뭐로 ____? (하다) ② 여기 ____? (앉다)
What do you say in Korean? Use a set phrase: ① Your friend's mother puts dinner on the table. You are about to eat. ② Your teacher explains the homework, and you understand.
answers: ① Guess ② Will ③ Guess ④ Will
① 피곤하겠어요 ② 무겁겠어요 ③ 바쁘겠어요
① 좋으겠어요 → 좋겠어요 ② 배고프겠어요 → 배고파요 (배가 고파요)
① 잘 먹겠습니다. ② 네, 알겠습니다.
